key_insight: Repeated SRF cavity cells retard incoming gas in staircase-like steps, while cavity traversal time follows a robust power law with vacuum-breach area.
engineering_relevance: The scaling law can guide isolation-system response times to limit contamination, heat deposition, and pressure buildup after vacuum loss.
method: Developed an experimentally validated multidimensional computational framework.
Coupled compressible gas dynamics, condensation, and cryogenic heat transfer.
Simulated a full-scale nine-cell SRF cavity across a broad range of breach sizes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental validation and robust traversal-time scaling across simulated breach sizes, but gives no numerical errors or scaling exponent.
watch_item: Mach-disk acoustic detection remains a proposed diagnostic that requires validation before operational deployment.
paper_title: Scaling laws for contamination traversal times during vacuum breaks in superconducting accelerators
